summary: Autonomous blended-wing-body delivery aircraft built around one-kilogram payloads.
editor_note: Small-package delivery is treated as an aircraft-efficiency problem: a 1.5 kg blended-wing-body vehicle carries roughly 1 kg for up to 40 km, launches vertically, and docks autonomously. Unlike adapting a quadcopter or road fleet, the narrow payload bet drives the whole airframe. The craft and operating loop earn the feature; certification and dense daily operations remain the hard proof points.

product_evidence.claim: Airbound describes a blended-wing-body tailsitter weighing about 1.5 kg, carrying roughly 1 kg, and targeting a 40 km range at 60 km/h.
The aircraft is designed for autonomous vertical launch, flight, and docking rather than requiring a runway or manual recovery.

market_context.primary_user: Logistics and commerce operators moving lightweight parcels across congested or road-poor routes.
market_context.differentiation: A lightweight fixed-wing airframe is optimized around the dominant one-kilogram delivery payload rather than a general-purpose drone.
market_context.why_now: Autonomy, battery performance, and rising last-mile costs make purpose-built small-package aircraft commercially testable.

risks.claim: Unit economics still depend on certification, reliability, and operating many aircraft per day in real airspace.
risks.basis: The Series A funds scale-up while the company moves from flight demonstrations toward dense commercial operations.
